record.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video and conversational editing
record.summary: Google announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on 5 November 2026 and says it is generally available through the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Google reports native video generation and editing up to 15 seconds, compared with 10 seconds for Omni 1.1, multi-turn conversational editing and a 30% price reduction to $0.07 per second for 720p generation. Google also claims stronger reference adherence and consistency, but the announcement provides no independent comparison. The release identifies continuing limitations for fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics; actual billed cost and quality across independent workloads remain unestablished.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google says Omni 1.2 Flash supports native video generation and editing up to 15 seconds, versus 10 seconds for Omni 1.1, and lists 720p generation at $0.07 per second, 30% below the prior model price.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google claims improved reference adherence and consistency across longer clips and multi-turn edits; no independent comparison or task-level quality results were inspected.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The release does not establish quality across independent workloads or realized billed cost. Google identifies ongoing limitations for fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched evaluation of reference adherence, temporal consistency or multi-turn editing was inspected.
The release states a per-second price but no realized billing, latency or iteration-count comparison.

brief.importance_rationale: If the announced release and price change hold, a generally available multimodal video model with native 15-second generation, conversational editing and a stated 30% price reduction can change product and cost choices for video workflows. This consequence score does not validate the provider-reported quality improvements.
limitations: The release is a provider announcement; its quality, consistency and workflow-efficiency statements are not independently validated here.
The $0.07/sec rate is a published price, not a measured total cost per successful clip or actual billed-cost comparison.
Google identifies fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics as continuing limitations.

technical.claimed_result: Google reports native video generation and editing up to 15 seconds, stronger reference adherence and multi-turn conversational editing. It lists $0.07 per second for 720p video, 30% below the previous price. These are provider statements; quality was not independently measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: Google’s dated 5 Nov 2026 announcement directly states general availability through the Gemini API and Gemini for business, a 15-second maximum versus 10 seconds for Omni 1.1, and the posted 720p rate of $0.07/sec.
technical.mechanism: The release describes native 15-second video generation, conversational multi-turn clip editing, and stronger conditioning on reference images, motion clips and audio cues.
technical.regime: Google’s announcement and stated product rollout; 720p price is $0.07 per second. No region-specific access check, model execution or realized billing was performed.
technical.reproducibility: The release and posted offer are directly inspectable. No independent model evaluation, controlled comparison or API call was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Google compares the maximum native clip duration with Omni 1.1 (15 seconds vs 10 seconds) and reports a 30% lower price. No matched independent quality or realized-cost baseline was obtained.
